- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.36) mid-period, model frequently fails to fully capture momentum; increase forecast slope or add 1–2% lagged momentum bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day smoothing filter on forecast to reduce sensitivity to sentiment swings.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >+5% above 18-day moving average, model often underestimates; add 1–2% bias to forecast to align with trend.
